title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
text: Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{γγ, γZ,γh\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8σ$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3σ$; strengthening to $2.7σ$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0σ$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7σ$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5σ$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4σ$; strengthening to $4.0σ$, $4.6σ$, and $6.1σ$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.

title: Recent Advances and Precision Measurements with the JYFLTRAP Double Penning Trap Mass Spectrometer
text: High-precision atomic-mass measurements with the JYFLTRAP double Penning-trap mass spectrometer at the IGISOL facility provide direct information on decay energies, nuclear binding and shell evolution, isomer excitation energies, and masses relevant to nuclear astrophysics. Recent work has combined the phase-imaging ion-cyclotron-resonance (PI-ICR) method with established ion-purification and selective ion-production techniques to study low-yield nuclei and resolve isomeric states. At JYFLTRAP/IGISOL, mass-selective buffer-gas cooling, Ramsey cleaning, resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS), phase-dependent cleaning, and species-resolved PI-ICR analysis are used in complementary combinations according to the ion yield and the required separation. Laser-frequency tagging correlates individual ion events with the corresponding laser frequency and enables state-resolved resonance-ionization spectra. Selected ion bunches are used for direct mass measurements with PI-ICR or time-of-flight ion-cyclotron resonance (TOF-ICR), for ion counting, or for post-trap decay spectroscopy. When multiple species or states are present, resolved PI-ICR phase spots allow the mass-measurement data to be assigned to the corresponding component. Examples from the recent program include high-precision $Q$-value measurements, neutron-deficient nuclei below $^{100}$Sn, neutron-rich fission fragments, rapid structural evolution around $N\approx60$, and rare-earth nuclei relevant to the astrophysical $r$ process.

title: Commissioning of GEM Detectors for the Super Bigbite Spectrometer
text: We report on the commissioning and cosmic characterization of the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) trackers for the recently completed first round of the Super Bigbite Spectrometer (SBS) experimental program conducted in Hall A of the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility. The SBS GEM trackers rank as one of the largest deployments of triple GEM detectors in operation and were critical to the success of the SBS program. Categorized by their readout strip orientation, the 56 individual SBS GEM modules range in active areas from 60cmx50cm (XY) to 150cmx40cm (UV, XW) and were fabricated at the University of Virginia. Large area layers were assembled from four XY GEM modules or a single UV or XW GEM module. The front-end electronics were based on APV25 chips with output sent to custom developed 40 MHz Multi-purpose Digitizers (MPDs). Prior to the installation of the GEM-based tracking systems for SBS experiments, the GEM modules underwent extensive cosmic-ray testing to characterize the performance of each module, including detector stability, efficiency, uniformity, timing performance, and spatial resolution.

title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
text: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026. We first apply PERC, short for Preprocessing (P), Embedding (E), Dimensionality Reduction (R) and Clustering (C). We employ GPT-6 Luna to classify job description passages into Team context, Role task and Qualifications. We then create combinations of these sections and examine whether embedding and clustering the segmented passages produce meaningful semantic clusters about different job roles. We use Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to rank observed differences between embedding distributions and employ a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to extract features from layer-19 representations of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Lastly, we employ GPT-6 Luna to come up with hypotheses about job roles' feature patterns, and GPT-6.1 Terra to investigate whether those patterns exist in held-out job descriptions from unseen companies. Some example findings include Data Scientist advertisements placing more emphasis on machine learning model development, Data Analyst advertisements on reporting business performance, and Machine Learning Engineer advertisements on applying developed models in real-world settings. We also observe differences in the applications described by Data Analyst and Business Analyst advertisements across selected months, although our dataset's scale and uneven coverage limit their interpretation. Overall, we present a realistic application of SAEs and PERC to unstructured textual data and examine how automated insight extraction could support manual analysis of job descriptions.

title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
text: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. We present CertiSum to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across runs, parallelism layouts, and GPU vendors. Its key insight is that native FP32 accumulation of MXFP4 products is often already exact for every summation order. CertiSum collects statistics during quantization to certify native matrix multiplication results, recomputes uncertified outputs exactly, and uses exact kernels directly where certification rarely succeeds. CertiSum keeps quantization blocks unchanged across layouts and merges partial sums without rounding, including in attention and weight-gradient computation. In 200-step Qwen3-8B-Base experiments, CertiSum preserves training states bit for bit across AMD MI350X and NVIDIA GB200 and across changes in data, tensor, and context parallelism on MI350X. Across three 8B--14B models on FineWeb-Edu using MI350X, it adds 11.8--60.5% to training-step latency relative to its non-exact MXFP4 counterpart at the larger evaluated input shapes, with speedups of up to $1.24\times$ over BF16 and $1.70\times$ over deterministic BF16.

title: Latent Lattice Language Models
text: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains. We introduce the Lattice of Latents, a set of per-layer horizontal latent streams that run recurrently along time, alongside the vertical residual stream that flows through depth. Like hyper-connections, mHC, and attention or value residuals, the Lattice enhances the residual stream, but rather than adding or rerouting residual pathways through depth, it provides companion computational states that persist across tokens. Unlike hybrid Transformer-SSM architectures, whose recurrent states primarily serve as internal memory for sequence mixing, these latents directly condition the vertical stream's attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. On Transformers trained on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, a 406M-parameter Lattice model lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 to 14.40 over a parameter-matched Transformer. These gains extend across architectural variants. The Lattice composes with prior residual-stream enhancements: with hyper-connections and input residuals, it lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 (base Transformer) and 14.22 (Transformer with the same enhancements) to 13.61. On Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2, Triadic GDN, and GDN-Mamba-2 hybrids, it improves perplexity at every tested native state size, with Lattice-GDN and Lattice-Triadic-GDN variants outperforming pure baselines with 4x larger native states. These results identify persistent per-layer state as a complementary axis for scaling language-model computation.

title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
text: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
text: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. A contrast set asks one question about several versions of an image that differ only in a small region with the evidence and have different answers, so only reading the evidence solves the whole set. CrossRPO rewards solving the whole set, and we prove that it does not reinforce a set answered from common sense. We build contrast sets for training (ViRA-Train) and evaluation (ViRA-Bench) by editing one small object in images of 21 to 120 megapixels, and we photograph further sets with real changes (ViRA-Bench-Real) to exclude editing traces. We train two Visual Reasoning Agents, ViRA-9B and ViRA-27B, with CrossRPO on only about 3,500 items of ViRA-Train each. CrossRPO achieves 63.3% set accuracy on ViRA-Bench at the maximum resolution, against 59.3% for GRPO. ViRA-9B is the most accurate open model of its size on all benchmarks, and ViRA-27B outperforms Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna, both at their highest thinking level, on most benchmarks.

title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
text: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
text: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors. For 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific tropical cyclones from the 2002-2023 hurricane seasons, we analyze the discussion text and its combination with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields, for forecasting intensity changes at lead times of 24 to 120 hours using three modeling methods. In one approach, an end-to-end deep learning framework for the text shows that the discussions alone offer comparable value for 24-hour intensity forecasts to the SHIPS predictors. Adding discussion information to the SHIPS predictors in an ensemble of five such models reduces the mean absolute error of 24-hour maximum sustained wind forecasts for 2022-2023 cyclones from 9.89 to 8.90 kt, with a confidence interval that excludes zero when whole storms are resampled. The ERA5 wind fields have a minor effect on mean absolute error in wind predictions, and model rankings differ across predicted variables, lead times and model types. title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
text: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region. Second, the same binding heads bind each written answer to the region it came from, and the model turns it into a progress signal: a cursor, the position in the image up to which the list has been written. Third, a select step chooses the nearest unwritten region after the cursor, or stops. Finally, gaze heads execute the chosen pointer and return a concept of what is drawn there, which language heads and the late MLPs turn into a word in the language of the question. We validate each part of this mechanism through causal patching in Qwen3-VL models on a synthetic visual retrieval task, and test our mechanisms against alternative hypotheses. We further show that the mechanism holds across input formats, natural photographs, and languages, and that its binding, relay, and gaze heads appear at every model size from 2B to 32B. This work allows us to investigate how a VLM turns a question and an image into a sequence of answers, layer by layer and token by token. More broadly, it opens a way to study how models plan over complex multi-step tasks with long rollouts. Our project is available at https://plan.baulab.info/

title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
text: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification problem as co-NP-complete, filling a key gap in the literature. Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-art verifiers.

title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
text: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regularization after the projector cannot correct it, and the differences between representations shrink until they collapse. We propose SADL (Supply And Demand Loss), which keeps the original training objective and constrains the encoder directly when needed. SADL compares the representation differences that the projector output demands with the differences the encoder can retain and pass on to the projector, and adds a constraint on the encoder only when supply falls short of demand. It works with different Demand Regularizers and introduces no auxiliary networks, additional trainable parameters, or architectural changes. In single-task and jointly trained four-task LeWorldModel (LeWM) and INTACT experiments, SADL lowers the collapse rate over ten random seeds from 50% to 0%. After one epoch of training, encoder effective rank is 3.4-6.4 times that of the corresponding baseline without SADL, and latent prediction error falls to 1/20-1/303 of it. Without additional tuning, SADL stays robust as its loss weight spans orders of magnitude, and with several Demand Regularizers INTACT exceeds 95% mean search-free control success. On four image datasets, SADL also consistently improves accuracy and stability across random seeds. These results show that matching the representation differences a regularizer demands with the differences the encoder can supply leads to faster and more stable representation learning in control and image classification.

title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design
text: Abstract Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP (“Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins”) for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

title: A scalable genomic framework for programmable strain tagging in a diverse bacterial genus
text: Abstract Inserting DNA into bacterial genomes is important to introduce or alter function for research and biotechnological applications. Transposons are widely used for this purpose, but commonly used systems such as Tn7, Tn5, and Mariner do not hit custom targets. CRISPR-associated transposons (CASTs) can direct the insertion of a transposon to chosen sites with short guide sequences, but their application outside of E. coli is still limited. We adapted CAST technology for use in the widespread plant-associated genus Sphingomonas, uniquely barcoding genetically diverse strains in two or more different sites, and we demonstrate the utility of the tags for quantitative strain tracking along with background microbiota in complex host-associated bacterial populations. During this work, comparative genomics revealed the canonical Tn7 insertion site frequently disrupts genes – and not only in Sphingomonas – suggesting Tn7 insertions may be more problematic than widely appreciated. Therefore, we identified improved loci downstream of genus-wide conserved sites, such as rpoZ in Sphingomonas and pyrD in Pseudomonas, as neutral alternatives. We experimentally validated the rpoZ locus in Sphingomonas and then targeted it in a heterogeneous uncharacterized Sphingomonas population. To support scalable screening, we introduce tagTIMseq, a rapid transposon mapping method that can identify on- and off-target insertions directly from single colonies. Together, these advances accelerate the creation of fully tagged synthetic communities for the high-throughput study of fine-scale bacterial natural variation.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
text: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: Pathophysiology-guided biomarkers and therapeutics for precision trauma medicine in polytrauma with musculoskeletal injuries
text: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. Conventional injury assessments, which rely heavily on anatomical scoring and nonspecific blood markers, fail to capture the dynamic molecular landscape underlying these conditions. To address this critical gap, we performed a comprehensive scoping review integrating evidence from basic science, translational studies, and clinical research published between January 2000 to June 2025, with particular emphasis on recent advances. The review highlights the discovery and validation of emerging blood-based and molecular biomarkers, including fatty acid-binding protein 3, syndecan-1, galectin-3, and trauma-associated microRNAs, as well as innovative diagnostic paradigms such as wearable biosensors, minimally invasive liquid biopsy platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics. Unlike prior reviews, our analysis uniquely integrates findings across both military and civilian trauma contexts, providing actionable frameworks for clinical application. Building on these insights, we outline a practical roadmap: 1) deploy integrated multi-marker panels for early risk stratification, 2) expand inclusive trauma biobanking to capture diverse injury phenotypes, and 3) use adaptive, data-driven tools for real-time triage and personalized intervention. This approach links acute systemic responses to downstream recovery and rehabilitation, offering actionable guidance for both military and civilian trauma systems.

title: Genetic variants in recurrent euploid pregnancy loss
text: Abstract Background Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) affects ~ 5% of couples. Known causes of RPL include aneuploidies and unbalanced chromosome rearrangements, however the genetic basis of losses with normal karyotype and chromosomal microarray analysis remains unclear. We hypothesized that deleterious variants in genes essential for early development, including genes previously associated only with neonatal lethal disorders, contribute to RPL. Methods Genome sequencing was performed on 118 families with unexplained, euploid RPL; 95% lacked major fetal structural anomalies on ultrasound. A tiered variant prioritization pipeline integrated model organism, human population databases, essential developmental pathways, and fetal transcriptomic profiles. Rare variants (allele frequency ≤ 0.1%) were assessed and confirmed by orthogonal methods. Parental samples were analyzed for mosaicism. Results Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants were identified in 18 families (15.3%) across 17 genes. These include six families with DHCR7 , PIEZO1 , PIGV , PRF1 , SLC12A3 , and SMN1 biallelic variants; two cases with ALAS2 and IKBKG hemizygous variants; and four pregnancies with heterozygous alterations inherited from affected parents with MYH3 and TNNI3 variants, and from asymptomatic parents with SCN5A and FLT4 variants. Additionally, four families had presumed de novo heterozygous variants in the EFTUD2 , HNRNPK , FGFR2 , and KAT6A genes (associated with autosomal dominant conditions), while two exhibited parental germline mosaicism in the FGFR2 and PORCN genes. Variants of uncertain significance were detected in 12 families (10.2%) across the ABCB7 , CLPB , CRB2 , FBN1 , FLT4 , GJA1 , LYST , MAGED2 , PTPN14 , RNF213 , TLR8 , and VPS35L genes. Of 28 genes with plausible variants, 13 genes were previously implicated in perinatal lethality, whereas 15 were novel candidates. Overall, variants in candidate genes were inherited in 80% of families. Four additional families (3.4%) had biallelic ultra-rare variants in genes, which are involved in fundamental developmental pathways but not yet linked to human disease, pointing to a possible role in prenatal lethality. Transcriptomic analyses supported novel gene involvement in hematopoiesis, cardiovascular development, inflammation, and fluid homeostasis processes. Conclusions Genome sequencing revealed plausible monogenic etiologies for unexplained euploid pregnancy loss, providing new insights into the biology of early human lethality, phenotypic spectra, recurrence risks, and inheritance patterns. These findings support expanding RPL diagnostics beyond karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis.

title: A transcriptomic atlas of grass senescence reveals divergent underground sink networks promote nitrogen recycling in perennials
text: Senescence enables plants to remobilize and recycle nutrients from aging organs to support growth, reproduction, and survival. In annual crops like maize, nitrogen remobilization from leaves to grain is incomplete, with 30-50% of nitrogen remaining in crop residue where it may be subject to environmental loss. Mitigating nitrogen loss in annual crops could be achieved by leveraging the physiological strategies of perennial grasses, which remobilize nitrogen and other nutrients into underground organs at the end of the growing season, thereby preventing environmental leakage. To uncover the molecular basis of perennial nitrogen recycling to underground organs, we built a transcriptomic atlas from field-grown plants, comprising 2,685 RNA-seq libraries from 14 grass species within the Panicoideae (Poaceae), utilizing maize and sorghum as annual references for comparative analyses. The atlas spans leaves, roots, stalks, and rhizomes across two seasons, from mid-growing season to senescence. Using a photosynthetic index to align the leaf's transition from nitrogen sink to source across species, co-expression network analysis revealed that the subnetworks driving leaf nitrogen remobilization are preserved across annuals and perennials. However, we discovered that the subnetworks associated with underground sink establishment, specifically those associated with seed-like dormancy and desiccation tolerance pathways, have diverged among annual crop accessions. Our work identifies conserved gene candidates and networks that could reintroduce perennial-like nutrient recycling into annual crops to enhance long-term nutrient retention in the field.

title: Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy
text: Histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previously, reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated H3K9ac were observed in placentas from women with preeclampsia. Building on these findings, this study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is associated with changes in placental histone modifications. Immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence were performed on placental sections from 60 patients stratified into four groups: women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed groups compared to unvaccinated controls, with the most pronounced reduction observed in women with prior infection during gestation. H3K9ac levels did not differ significantly between groups in any compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between SCT H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight, and a sensitivity analysis excluding cases with additional placental pathologies confirmed the robustness of the findings. As no gene expression profiling was performed, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 changes cannot be inferred. These descriptive findings warrant further investigation integrating epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches to clarify their functional relevance for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
text: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: Pathophysiology-guided biomarkers and therapeutics for precision trauma medicine in polytrauma with musculoskeletal injuries
text: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. Conventional injury assessments, which rely heavily on anatomical scoring and nonspecific blood markers, fail to capture the dynamic molecular landscape underlying these conditions. To address this critical gap, we performed a comprehensive scoping review integrating evidence from basic science, translational studies, and clinical research published between January 2000 to June 2025, with particular emphasis on recent advances. The review highlights the discovery and validation of emerging blood-based and molecular biomarkers, including fatty acid-binding protein 3, syndecan-1, galectin-3, and trauma-associated microRNAs, as well as innovative diagnostic paradigms such as wearable biosensors, minimally invasive liquid biopsy platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics. Unlike prior reviews, our analysis uniquely integrates findings across both military and civilian trauma contexts, providing actionable frameworks for clinical application. Building on these insights, we outline a practical roadmap: 1) deploy integrated multi-marker panels for early risk stratification, 2) expand inclusive trauma biobanking to capture diverse injury phenotypes, and 3) use adaptive, data-driven tools for real-time triage and personalized intervention. This approach links acute systemic responses to downstream recovery and rehabilitation, offering actionable guidance for both military and civilian trauma systems.

title: Benchmarking machine learning and molecular dynamics methods for the prediction of the thermophysical properties of organic liquids
text: Machine learning models trained on ∼4700 reference values predict the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of lubricant-sized organic molecules, benchmarked against Green–Kubo molecular dynamics simulations of eight representative fluids.

title: Beyond Organisational Accidents: Safety Causation and Sociological Explanation
text: Beyond Organisational Accidents: Safety Causation and Sociological Explanation is a tribute to James Reason and a contribution to the sociology of safety. Reason’s theories defined a new era in the safety field in the 1980s and 1990s but, as time passes, our understanding and knowledge of any topic evolves. Different proposals are made, new perspectives develop, alternatives are suggested. The same is true for Reason’s contribution and several decades after his landmark publications, our view of human error, of organisational accidents and of safe performance have evolved. In the 2020s, our approach to this problem is not the same as it was back then. This book explores the alternatives by drawing on fifty years of developments in different traditions such as cognitive system engineering. It investigates the thoughts of Rasmussen, Hollnagel and Woods who shaped what is known as the “ new view ” and sociology through the perspectives of Perrow, Hopkins, Vaughan and McCurdy. It argues that safety issues associated with complex and globalised organisations such as Boeing, NASA, SpaceX or a global event such as the COVID-19 pandemic require a revisit of the classics in the safety field. In this respect, the book builds on, refines and expands upon the ideas set out in the author's previous publication, Post Normal Accident (ISBN: 9780367502287), marking a shift in focus from accident causation to safety causation. This book is an essential resource for occupational health and safety professionals, researchers, and students. Its appeal extends to those in the disciplines of human factors, ergonomics, and sociology. It is particularly valuable for those working with complex, high-risk systems who seek a deeper theoretical foundation to guide their practices.

title: An IMU Dataset for Human Activity Recognition to Support Independent Living in Smart Homes (IMU-HAR-IL)
text: Abstract The majority of existing human activity recognition (HAR) datasets rely on wearable or object-mounted inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors, yet they fall short in a critical dimension – they are not purposefully designed to capture the specific activities that serve as meaningful indicators of independent living among older adults. This document introduces HAR-IMU-IL, a dataset developed for HAR using IMU sensors within a smart home environment with a focus to support objective functional assessment of older adults’ independent living (IL). In particular, HAR-IMU-IL includes recordings of 50 participants performing 17 clinically relevant activities of daily living, spanning 4 functional domains essential for independent living: mobility, hygiene, nutrition and hydration, and medication intake. The dataset was collected using 30 IMU sensors, comprising both wearable and object-mounted devices integrated within a real-world residential setting. The dataset includes multi-sensor inertial data captured under realistic, unconstrained conditions, together with detailed annotations ensuring high temporal accuracy and consistency across sensors. A comprehensive data collection protocol was implemented to preserve ecological validity and enable reliable multi-sensor synchronisation. HAR-IMU-IL provides a large-scale, functionally grounded resource for advancing and benchmarking machine learning and artificial intelligence approaches for HAR in home settings. Its utility is further demonstrated by developing models capable of accurately recognising both activities and broader functional areas using wearable and object-mounted sensors. These capabilities highlight potential of the dataset to enable applications in continuous activity monitoring, functional health assessment, smart home automation, and assistive technologies that support independent living. By bridging the gap between raw motion sensing and semantic understanding of human activities, this work advances a foundational capability with broad implications for bioengineering systems design, robotic assistance, and clinical rehabilitation, where accurate, real-time recognition of purposeful human action is essential for responsive, adaptive, and personalised interventions.

title: Cartesian gantry robots for light-payload pick-and-place, storage-and-retrieval and laboratory automation: a PRISMA 2020 systematic review of architectures, transmissions, motion control and reported performance (2010–2026)
text: Cartesian gantry robots (XY, XYZ, H-bot, CoreXY and dual-drive gantries with payloads up to about 50 kg) are widely used for pick-and-place, automated storage and retrieval, assembly and laboratory automation. No systematic, protocol-driven review synthesises the performance they are reported to achieve. The closest recent review is narrative and covers modelling and virtual prototyping. This systematic review maps and synthesises the peer-reviewed evidence from 2010 to 2026 on gantry architectures, transmissions and motion control, and on how their performance is measured and reported. It then proposes a benchmarking and reporting framework derived from the gaps it finds. It follows PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S and SWiM.

title: Pathophysiology-guided biomarkers and therapeutics for precision trauma medicine in polytrauma with musculoskeletal injuries
text: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. To address this critical gap, we performed a comprehensive scoping review integrating evidence from basic science, translational studies, and clinical research published between January 2000 to June 2025, with particular emphasis on recent advances.
